An RSA key this process holds only the public half of. Creating a signature is handed to a delegate — typically a call to the vault or module that keeps the private half.

Remarks

It is an RsaSecurityKey so that everything that publishes or verifies with the public parameters — a JWKS endpoint, a token validator — keeps working unchanged. Only the creation of a signature is redirected, through the key's own CryptoProviderFactory.

Signatures are RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256 (RS256); the delegate receives the data to sign, not a digest, and returns the signature.
